domains.description: Search and inspect Moodle command/API manifest entries.
Profile setup, device-flow login, auth status, and logout.
Diagnose config, token, service, and Moodle capability problems.
Read courses, activities, resources, grades, progress, and notifications.
Read Moodle question categories, search questions, pick random questions, and render question HTML.
Quiz listing, native practice quiz creation, attempt lifecycle, and structured answering.
List Moodle calendar events and publish/upsert study plan events.
Read assignment status, save drafts, and submit final work.
Read discussions and create/reply/update/delete forum posts.

repairHints: If the catalog call fails, run doctor.check and auth.status.
Run auth.login_start after setup to obtain a token.

noWait.description: Return a verification URL instead of waiting interactively.

repairHints: Give the returned verification_url and user_code to the user in headless sessions.
If token is missing or invalid, run auth.login_start.
If no profiles exist, run auth.setup first.
Use auth.list_profiles first if the profile name is uncertain.
Use auth.status before logout if you only need to inspect current auth state.
Use this before retrying a failing write command.
If token is missing, run auth.status then auth.login_start.
If no courses are returned, check enrollment and token user identity.
If the course is not visible, check enrollment and role permissions.

modname.description: Optional Moodle module type filter, such as quiz or assign.

repairHints: If a known module is missing, check activity visibility and course permissions.
If detail lookup fails, confirm the cmid from course.outline or course.list_activities.
If due items are missing, verify course activity due/open/completion expected dates.
If resources are empty, call course.outline to inspect visible modules.
If grades are unavailable, check gradebook visibility and user role.
If progress is unavailable, check completion tracking settings for the course.
If notifications are empty, check the target user and Moodle notification settings.
If categories are empty, check question bank permissions and course context.

tagIds.description: Moodle native question tag ids to require. Use questionbank.tags first to discover tag ids.

repairHints: If search returns no rows, call questionbank.categories to confirm category ids and context.
If you need tag ids, call questionbank.tags after running questionbank.tags_sync for the course/category.
If tags are empty after Moodle question tags were edited, run questionbank.tags_sync for the course/category.
This command only rebuilds local_aiagentapi_qtagidx from Moodle native question tags; it does not change Moodle question tags.
If not enough questions are returned, search the category and consider recurse or broader qtype filters.
Use questionbank.search or questionbank.pick_random to discover question ids first.
If no quizzes are returned, call course.outline and check course visibility.

copies.description: Number of randomized copies to resolve.

repairHints: Use this to inspect Moodle-native random slots without creating an attempt.
Use this before starting a new attempt to avoid unnecessary duplicate attempts.
Use attempt_data to inspect response schema before calling quiz.answer.
Use this before final submission to show what will be submitted.

categoryIds.description: Repeatable Moodle question category ids. Category ids are source locations; use tags to express teaching scope.

tags.description: Teaching tag filters. Prefer large chapter tags such as 第一章 for broad filtering plus small section tags such as 1.3 or 集合的基本运算 for focus.

tagIds.description: Moodle native question tag ids to require. Use questionbank.tags to discover ids.

allowPartial.description: Create with fewer than count questions when necessary.

visible.description: Make the created quiz visible to students.

examples: python3 scripts/moodle_cli.py --profile dzexam --json --dry-run quiz create-practice --idempotency-key <key> --course-id 116 --category-id 619 --category-id 616 --tag "第一章" --tag "1.3" --count 30 --random
repairHints: For mixed-category quiz creation, treat category ids as source locations and tags as the teaching filter.
Use questionbank.tags to discover Moodle tag ids when random mode must preserve tag filters.
Use a broad chapter tag such as 第一章 first, add a small-section tag such as 1.3 when needed, then inspect dry-run questions[].categoryid, qtype, and name.
If creation fails with permission errors, check local/aiagentapi:use and quiz/question bank capabilities.
If count validation fails, current supported maximum is 120.
If no quiz id is known, call quiz.list first.
Prefer quiz.answer for supported choice questions; use save_attempt only when raw Moodle response names are known.

responses.description: Optional Moodle raw response name/value pairs.

repairHints: Call quiz.attempt_summary before submitting so the user can review the final state.

answers.description: Structured supported-answer objects, such as slot plus choice_index/choice_indexes.

repairHints: Use quiz.attempt_data first; quiz.answer supports only response schemas that the CLI can normalize safely.
Use course.due for activity due/open/completion timestamps; use calendar.list for calendar events.
Preview with dry-run first; calendar writes create user-visible events.
Use upsert_plan when the caller has a stable plan key and wants repeatable updates.
Use course.list_activities with modname=assign if you need mixed activity context.
Check assignment status before saving or submitting.
Save draft is reversible by editing the draft, but still changes student-visible submission state.
Submit final should only run after explicit user confirmation because it can lock or finalize grading state.
Use this before replying so the target post/discussion is clear.
Forum posts are user-visible; preview and confirm the exact text before writing.

privateReply.description: Create a private reply when supported.

repairHints: Confirm the parent post id from forum.discussions before replying.
Only update posts after confirming the target post id and intended replacement text.
Only use after explicit user request and permission confirmation. Actual delete requires allowDestructive=true.
